display.title: Where Has My Story Gone? Part 1
display.summary_short: The Baal Shem Tov's attendant, Reb Yaakov, becomes a traveling storyteller, but in the home of a wealthy Jew in Rome he suddenly cannot remember a single story.
display.summary_long: After the song "I believe in Hashem", the storyteller explains why Chassidim repeat stories: like the Megillah and the weekly parsha, each hearing brings new lessons as we grow. Before his passing, the Baal Shem Tov gives each student a mission, and tells his attendant, Reb Yaakov, to travel and tell what they experienced together. Reb Yaakov becomes a beloved wandering maggid, coming home only for Yom Tov. When his wife begs him to settle down, he answers that he will stop only when the Baal Shem Tov gives him a sign; the storyteller notes how the Rebbe told Chassidim to keep writing to the Frierdiker Rebbe after his passing. Hearing of a wealthy community head in Rome, Reb Moshe, who pays generously for stories of the Baal Shem Tov, Reb Yaakov travels there and is warmly welcomed. But at the Friday night gathering his mind goes blank, and the same happens at every meal of Shabbos and at Melave Malka, while the crowd begins to doubt him. Reb Moshe begs him to stay until Tuesday. As Reb Yaakov sits down in his wagon to leave, he suddenly cries out that he remembers one story. To be continued.
display.lesson: Stories of tzaddikim are worth hearing again and again, because each time we can learn a new lesson; a Chassid keeps doing his mission until the Rebbe signals otherwise.
